correctness.rationale: Positive definiteness is exactly nonnegativity of unnormalized Walsh coefficients. Coordinate averaging proves the sharp bound and the radial feasible equality point. At the minimal Krawtchouk levels every nonnegative Fourier coefficient must vanish. Filmus’s full harmonic slice basis gives a direct-sum decomposition for supports of weight four, and exact pair-contrast summation diagonalizes the restricted Walsh operator with multipliers K4, −t(t²−3d+8)/3, 2(t²−d+4), −8t, 16. The quadratic expression in t² proves the minimizing weights lie in [4,d−4] for d≥13, and all nonconstant multipliers there are nonzero except possibly degree one exactly when t²=3d−8; this is the stated square-resonance locus. Explicit remaining Fourier inequalities are necessary/sufficient and strictly slack off minimizing levels, proving a full (d−1)-dimensional optimizer polytope there, unique radial otherwise. Exact checker on the packaged path passed 5,115 formula identities, 988 dimension classifications, 16,438 contrast instances, and 72 rational inequalities of a dimension-19 nonradial witness. Finite computations support but do not establish the infinite theorem.

originality.rationale: The specific new claim is the complete optimizer geometry for support at Hamming weight four, especially the arithmetic square-resonance family and explicit full-dimensional nonradial equality face. value.rationale: The fixed-weight-four Hamming shell is a canonical finite harmonic-analysis support, not an arbitrary computational slice. The theorem determines the entire sharp positive-definite extremizer set uniformly in d≥13, including the surprising infinite arithmetic jump from a single radial optimizer to a full (d−1)-dimensional nonradial face at d=19,24,36,43,59,…. This materially refines the sharp scalar constant, gives exact inequalities for constructing all extremizers and distinguishes fourth-shell resonance from known weight-two parity behavior. It is a natural complete classification rather than a routine substitution or small numerical gain.
